questions.question: What was the overall unemployment rate in India as reported in the 6ₜₕ Annual Employment-Unemployment Survey conducted by the Labour Bureau?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**5.4**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The 6th Annual Employment-Unemployment Survey (2016-17) by the Labour Bureau reported the overall unemployment rate in India as **5.4% (0.054).**
 
• The survey highlighted a higher unemployment rate among women (8.7%) compared to men (4.0%).
 
• Rural unemployment stood at 5.1%, while urban unemployment was slightly higher at 5.8%.
 
• The survey aimed to provide detailed insights into employment patterns, labor force participation, and unemployment trends across various demographics.
 
• The report is considered a critical source for policymaking in addressing employment challenges in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Unemployment Rate:**

 
 
• It refers to the percentage of individuals in the labor force who are unable to find jobs despite actively seeking work.
 
• Unemployment is categorized into types such as structural, frictional, cyclical, and seasonal unemployment.
 
 
 
• **Labour Bureau Surveys:**
 
 
• The Labour Bureau, under the Ministry of Labour and Employment, conducts these surveys to assess employment and unemployment trends in India.
 
• The surveys are critical in identifying challenges in the labor market and formulating evidence-based policies.
 
 
 
• **Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS):**
 
 
• Since 2017-18, the PLFS by the National Statistical Office (NSO) has replaced the Labour Bureau surveys for better and more frequent labor market data.
 
• PLFS provides quarterly estimates for urban areas and annual estimates for both rural and urban regions.
 
 
 
• **Labor Force Participation Rate (LFPR):**
 
 
• It is the percentage of the working-age population that is either employed or actively seeking employment.
 
• India's LFPR has historically been low, particularly for women, due to various social, economic, and cultural factors.
 
 
 
• **Policy Interventions:**
 
 
• The Indian government has launched schemes like MGNREGA, Skill India, and Start-Up India to address unemployment and enhance skill development.
 
• These initiatives aim to provide employment opportunities and promote entrepreneurship among the youth.

questions.question: In February 2025, Muthoot Finance has received RBI approval to open how many new branches across India, strengthening its presence in the gold loan market?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**115**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In February 2025, Muthoot Finance received approval from the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) to open **115 new branches** across the country.
 
• This strategic expansion aims to strengthen Muthoot Finance's presence in the **gold loan market**, a key segment in India's financial sector.
 
• The approval aligns with Muthoot Finance's vision to broaden its reach, especially in **rural and semi-urban areas**, to cater to the growing demand for gold loans.
 
• Muthoot Finance is the largest gold financing company in India, with a market share of over **20%** in the organized gold loan market.
 
• The new branches will enhance access to financial services, including **gold loans, insurance, and money transfer services**, among underserved populations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gold Loan Market in India:**

 
 
• India is one of the largest consumers of gold globally, with households holding over **25,000 tons** of gold, making gold loans a popular financial product.
 
• Gold loans are secured loans where borrowers pledge their gold jewelry or ornaments as collateral.
 
• The organized gold loan market in India is dominated by NBFCs like Muthoot Finance and Manappuram Finance, along with banks.
 
 
 
• **Muthoot Finance Overview:**
 
 
• Muthoot Finance Limited is a leading Non-Banking Financial Company (NBFC) in India, founded in 1939.
 
• It specializes in **gold loans, money transfer services, investment products, and insurance services**.
 
• With a vast network of branches, Muthoot Finance primarily caters to rural and semi-urban customers.
 
 
 
• **RBI's Role in Branch Approvals:**
 
 
• The Reserve Bank of India regulates NBFCs and approves their expansion plans, ensuring adherence to financial and operational guidelines.
 
• Branch expansions are approved based on factors such as financial health, compliance history, and market demand.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Branch Expansion:**
 
 
• Branch expansions improve financial inclusion by providing easier access to loans and other financial services in underbanked areas.
 
• They also contribute to **employment generation** and support regional economic growth.

questions.question: Which initiative was launched on 25 September 2014 to facilitate investment, foster innovation, build best in class infrastructure and make India a hub for manufacturing, design and innovation?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Make in India initiative**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Make in India initiative** was launched by the Government of India on **25 September 2014**, under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi.
 
• It aims to transform India into a global manufacturing hub by **encouraging domestic and foreign investment** in manufacturing sectors.
 
• The initiative focuses on fostering innovation, enhancing skill development, and building world-class infrastructure.
 
• It targets **25 key sectors**, including automobiles, biotechnology, construction, defense manufacturing, and pharmaceuticals, among others.
 
• The program emphasizes ease of doing business by streamlining regulatory frameworks, promoting transparency, and simplifying processes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **FDI Reforms:**

 
 
• Under Make in India, India liberalized its **Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) policies** across various sectors, allowing up to 100% FDI in many industries.
 
• Sectors like defense, railways, and insurance witnessed increased FDI inflows due to policy reforms.
 
 
 
• **Ease of Doing Business Ranking:**
 
 
• India’s global position in the World Bank's **Ease of Doing Business Index** improved significantly due to initiatives under Make in India.
 
• Key reforms include the introduction of GST, Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, and digitization of governance processes.
 
 
 
• **Major Outcomes:**
 
 
• Significant growth in sectors like electronics, automotive, and renewable energy.
 
• India became one of the fastest-growing economies globally, attracting substantial foreign investments.
 
 
 
• **Skill India Initiative:**
 
 
• To complement Make in India, the **Skill India program** focuses on enhancing workforce employability through training and skill development.
 
• This ensures a skilled labor pool to meet the demands of the manufacturing and service sectors.

questions.question: Which of the following indicators reflects inequality in the distribution of income among individuals in a population?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lorenz Curve**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Lorenz Curve is a graphical representation that illustrates the distribution of income or wealth among individuals or households in a population.
 
• It is used to measure income inequality, where the degree of deviation from the line of perfect equality (the diagonal line) indicates the level of inequality.
 
• The closer the Lorenz Curve is to the diagonal line, the more equal the income distribution; the farther it is, the greater the inequality.
 
• The curve is often used in conjunction with the Gini Coefficient, which quantifies the level of income inequality as a single numerical value.
 
• Developed by Max Lorenz in 1905, this tool remains a cornerstone in economic studies related to inequality and social welfare.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gini Coefficient:**

 
 
• The Gini Coefficient is a numerical measure derived from the Lorenz Curve, ranging from 0 to 1.
 
• A Gini Coefficient of 0 indicates perfect equality, while a value of 1 indicates perfect inequality.
 
• It is widely used by economists and policymakers to compare income inequality across regions or countries.
 
 
 
• **Dependency Ratio:**
 
 
• This is a demographic metric that indicates the ratio of dependents (young and elderly) to the working-age population.
 
• While important for understanding economic pressures, it does not measure income inequality.
 
 
 
• **Consumer Price Index (CPI):**
 
 
• CPI measures changes in the price level of a basket of consumer goods and services purchased by households over time.
 
• It is a key indicator of inflation, not income distribution.
 
 
 
• **Labour Force Participation Rate (LFPR):**
 
 
• LFPR measures the proportion of the working-age population that is either employed or actively seeking employment.
 
• It provides insights into labor market dynamics but does not reflect income inequality.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context of Income Inequality Studies:**
 
 
• The study of income inequality gained prominence during the 20th century as economists sought to understand its implications on economic growth and social stability.
 
• Tools like the Lorenz Curve and Gini Coefficient remain fundamental to these analyses.

questions.question: After independence, co-operatives became an integral part of which planning initiative in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Five-Year Plans.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Co-operatives became an integral part of the Five-Year Plans in India, as they were seen as a crucial mechanism for socio-economic development.**
 
• **The First Five-Year Plan (1951-1956) emphasized agricultural development and rural reconstruction, where cooperatives were actively promoted.**
 
• **Cooperatives were considered essential for pooling resources, improving agricultural productivity, and ensuring equitable distribution of profits among farmers.**
 
• **Over the years, the cooperative movement expanded into sectors like banking, housing, dairy, and marketing, playing a vital role in economic growth.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Industrial Policy Resolution:** The Industrial Policy Resolutions of 1948 and 1956 were focused on laying the foundation for India's industrial development. They categorized industries into private, public, and joint sectors to enable planned industrial growth. While cooperative societies were mentioned, they were not the central focus.
 
• **Green Revolution:** The Green Revolution in India (1960s) aimed at increasing agricultural productivity through the introduction of high-yielding variety seeds, fertilizers, and irrigation techniques. Though cooperatives played a role in distribution, the initiative primarily revolved around technological advancements in agriculture.
 
• **Operation Flood:** Operation Flood, launched in 1970 by the National Dairy Development Board (NDDB), was aimed at increasing milk production in India. It was a significant initiative to create a nationwide milk grid, which heavily relied on dairy cooperatives but was focused solely on the dairy sector.

questions.question: In which year did the National Development Council (NDC) recommend a national policy on co-operatives?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**1958**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **National Development Council (NDC)** was established in 1952 as an advisory body to strengthen and mobilize the effort and resources for the country's development.
 
• In **1958**, the NDC recognized the importance of **co-operative societies** in fostering economic and social development in India.
 
• It recommended the formulation of a **national policy on co-operatives** to ensure their effective role in achieving socio-economic objectives like rural development and poverty alleviation.
 
• The **co-operative movement** in India has a long history, and its aim is to promote self-help and mutual aid among its members.
 
• Co-operatives played a critical role in **agriculture, credit institutions, rural industries, and marketing**, which were crucial for post-independence development.
 
• The recommendation in 1958 was instrumental in expanding the co-operative sector with the support of the government, leading to the establishment of laws like the **Multi-State Co-operative Societies Act, 2002**.
 
• This policy emphasized the need for **autonomy, democratic management, and economic viability** of co-operatives.
 
• It also advocated for the creation of an enabling environment for co-operatives to thrive as self-reliant and sustainable entities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **1947**__

 __
 
• This was the year of **India's independence**, and the focus of the government was on nation-building and planning for economic development.
 
• While co-operatives existed before independence, no specific recommendation for a national policy was made in this year.
 
 
 
• **1962**__
 __
 
• This year marked the initiation of the **Third Five-Year Plan**, focusing on agricultural development, but it was not the year when the NDC recommended a national co-operative policy.
 
• By this time, co-operatives were already being implemented in areas like credit and rural development.
 
 
 
• **1975**__
 
 
• This year is significant for the introduction of the **Twenty-Point Programme** by the Government of India, which also included co-operatives under rural development schemes.
 
• However, this was not the year of the NDC's recommendation for a national policy on co-operatives.

questions.question: What was the budget allocated in the Smart City Mission for the financial year 2023-24?

• This fund is utilized for developing **100 smart cities across India** with focus on **smart solutions** like better urban mobility, improved sanitation, and efficient energy use.
 
• Under the mission, cities aim to use **technology, governance, and innovation** to address urban challenges.
 
• Projects funded include **integrated command and control centers, waste management systems, and smart transportation networks**.

 __

questions.question: Which of the following is an indirect tax levied in India?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Goods and Services Tax**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Goods and Services Tax (GST)** is an **indirect tax** implemented in **India** on July 1, 2017.
 
• It is a comprehensive, multi-stage, destination-based tax that is levied on every value addition.
 
• GST replaced multiple indirect taxes like **Central Excise Duty, Service Tax, VAT, and others.**
 
• It is governed by the **Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017**, and is categorized into **Central GST (CGST), State GST (SGST), and Integrated GST (IGST).**
 
• GST ensures a uniform tax structure across the country and eliminates the cascading effect of taxes.
 
• Under GST, consumers pay tax only on the value added to goods or services.
 
• It is implemented under the constitutional framework of **Article 246A** of the Indian Constitution, which grants powers to both the Parliament and State Legislatures to make laws regarding GST.
 
• GST applies to goods and services at different rates: **0%, 5%, 18%, and 40%**, depending on the category.
 
• The introduction of GST has simplified the taxation system, promoted ease of doing business, and enhanced tax compliance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Equalisation Levy**__

 __
 
• The **Equalisation Levy**, also known as the **Google Tax**, was introduced in **India** in **2016** to tax digital transactions.
 
• It aims to address taxation challenges posed by the digital economy, specifically targeting companies like Google, Facebook, and other online platforms.
 
• The levy is not considered a broad-based indirect tax like GST but is a targeted tax primarily applied to **non-resident companies** providing online advertising services.
 
 
 
• **Capital Gain Tax**__
 __
 
• **Capital Gain Tax** is a **direct tax** levied on the profit earned from the sale of a capital asset, such as property, stocks, or bonds.
 
• It is categorized into **short-term capital gains** and **long-term capital gains** based on the holding period of the asset.
 
• This tax is not an indirect tax and is paid directly by the individual or entity earning the profit.
 
 
 
• **Corporate Tax**__
 
 
• **Corporate Tax** is a **direct tax** imposed on the income or profit of corporations and companies.
 
• It is calculated on the net income after expenses and deductions as per the **Income Tax Act, 1961**.
 
• Corporate Tax rates vary based on the type of company, such as domestic or foreign, and its turnover.

questions.question: Which industry is closely associated with 'cluster development' and the second-largest sector in terms of job creation in India after agriculture?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Textile and Apparel**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The textile and apparel industry is the **second-largest sector in India** in terms of job creation, after agriculture.
 
• Cluster development is a widely used strategy in this sector to **promote competitiveness and regional specialization**.
 
• The Indian textile and apparel industry contributes significantly to the **GDP, export earnings, and employment generation**.
 
• India is one of the world's largest producers of textiles and garments, with a strong presence in cotton, silk, and jute production.
 
• The industry is highly labor-intensive, employing over **45 million people directly** and around 60 million indirectly.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Cluster Development**

 
 
• Cluster development involves **grouping enterprises within a specific geographic location** to promote shared resources, collaboration, and innovation.
 
• It enhances productivity, competitiveness, and economies of scale for small and medium enterprises (SMEs).
 
• This approach is particularly effective in labor-intensive industries like textiles and apparel.
 
 
 
• **Contribution to Exports**
 
 
• The textile and apparel industry accounts for approximately **12% of India’s total export earnings**.
 
• India is a leading exporter of cotton textiles, garments, and home furnishings globally.
 
 
 
• **Government Initiatives**
 
 
• Programs like **Integrated Textile Parks** and **Technology Upgradation Fund Scheme (TUFS)** aim to support the industry.
 
• The **National Technical Textiles Mission** was launched to enhance the use of technical textiles in India.
 
 
 
• **Employment Generation**
 
 
• The textile sector is a major source of employment, providing jobs to millions, particularly women in rural areas.
 
• It plays a critical role in **poverty alleviation and rural development** in India.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the Five-Year Plans of India. Which of these statements is/are correct?

1. The First Five-Year Plan was based on the Harrod-Domar model and it prioritised agricultural development to address food security.

2. The Second Five-Year Plan, known as the Mahalanobis Plan, focussed on rapid industrialisation.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 3: Both Statement 1 and Statement 2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Statement 1 is correct:** The First Five-Year Plan (1951-1956) was based on the Harrod-Domar growth model and emphasised agricultural development to address food shortages and achieve food security.
 
• The plan focused on **agriculture, irrigation, and land reforms** to rebuild the agrarian economy after independence.
 
• **Statement 2 is correct:** The Second Five-Year Plan (1956-1961), also known as the Mahalanobis Plan, prioritised **industrialisation**, particularly heavy industries, to build the foundation for long-term economic growth.
 
• The Mahalanobis Model advocated increasing the share of investment in industries producing capital goods, with a focus on public sector enterprises.
 
• Both plans played a crucial role in shaping India’s economic development trajectory during its early years of independence.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Harrod-Domar Model:** This economic model emphasises the relationship between savings, investment, and economic growth. It was chosen for the First Five-Year Plan to address India’s immediate post-independence challenges, like food shortages and inflation.
 
• **Mahalanobis Model:** Named after economist P.C. Mahalanobis, this model guided the Second Five-Year Plan. It prioritised capital goods industries to create a base for self-reliant economic growth.
 
• **Five-Year Plans:** India adopted the concept of centralised economic planning inspired by the Soviet Union. The Planning Commission was established in 1950 to oversee the formulation and implementation of these plans.
 
• **Public Sector Focus:** The Second Five-Year Plan emphasised public sector enterprises to achieve industrialisation, reduce dependency on imports, and create infrastructure for long-term growth.
 
• **Transition to NITI Aayog:** The Planning Commission was replaced by NITI Aayog in 2015. The five-year planning framework was discontinued, and a more decentralised approach to planning was adopted.

questions.question: What was the estimated capital expenditure of the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways in India for the financial year 2024-25?

__
 
• The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) in India had an estimated capital expenditure of **₹2.72 lakh crore** for the financial year 2024-25.
 
• This allocation aimed to accelerate the construction of national highways and improve road infrastructure across the country.
 
• The increased budget allocation was part of the Indian government's focus on enhancing connectivity and supporting economic growth.
 
• The capital expenditure for MoRTH has been steadily increasing in recent years, reflecting the government's commitment to infrastructure development.
 
• This funding supports projects such as the Bharatmala Pariyojana, aimed at developing economic corridors and expressways.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bharatmala Pariyojana:**

 
 
• A flagship program launched by the Indian government to develop highways and economic corridors across the country.
 
• It aims to improve freight movement, reduce travel time, and enhance overall connectivity.
 
• The program includes the construction of expressways, bridges, and bypasses to boost infrastructure.
 
 
 
• **National Infrastructure Pipeline (NIP):**
 
 
• The NIP is a government initiative aimed at providing world-class infrastructure across India.
 
• It includes projects in sectors like transportation, energy, water, and communication.
 
• Road infrastructure plays a significant role in the NIP, with substantial funding allocated to MoRTH projects.
 
 
 
• **Gati Shakti Master Plan:**
 
 
• Launched by the Indian government to integrate and coordinate infrastructure projects for seamless connectivity.
 
• This initiative focuses on the synergy between road, rail, air, and waterways for effective logistics management.
 
 
 
• **Public-Private Partnerships (PPP) in Road Infrastructure:**
 
 
• India extensively uses PPP models for road construction and maintenance to ensure efficient project execution.
 
• PPP models like Build-Operate-Transfer (BOT) and Hybrid Annuity Model (HAM) are widely adopted.

questions.question: Which revolution in India is associated with the growth of the fishing industry?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Blue Revolution**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Blue Revolution** is associated with the **growth of the fishing industry** in India.
 
• It refers to the significant increase in the production of **fish and marine products** through advanced techniques such as **aquaculture** and better management practices.
 
• The revolution aimed to improve **aquatic resources** and ensure better utilization of water bodies for fish farming.
 
• The **Fish Farmers Development Agency (FFDA)** and **National Fisheries Development Board** were key organizations that supported the initiatives under the Blue Revolution.
 
• The Blue Revolution also focused on enhancing **employment opportunities** in the fisheries sector, benefitting rural and coastal communities.
 
• India became one of the world's largest producers of fish due to the initiatives under this revolution, contributing significantly to its **food security** and **export earnings**.
 
• The Blue Revolution is crucial for ensuring sustainable management of aquatic ecosystems while meeting the growing demand for **fish and seafood**.
 
• It also included the development of **marine fisheries**, **inland fisheries**, and **brackish water aquaculture**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **White Revolution**__

 __
 
• The **White Revolution** in India is associated with the **production and growth of milk**.
 
• This revolution was spearheaded by **Dr. Verghese Kurien**, known as the father of the White Revolution.
 
• It led to India becoming the largest producer of milk in the world and promoted **self-sufficiency in dairy production**.
 
• The initiative was implemented through the **Operation Flood** program launched by the **National Dairy Development Board (NDDB)**.
 
• The White Revolution contributed significantly to improving **nutrition levels**, enhancing **livelihoods**, and reducing dependency on imports.
 
 
 
• **Green Revolution**__
 __
 
• The **Green Revolution** refers to the significant increase in **agricultural production** in India during the 1960s and 1970s.
 
• It focused on the use of **high-yield variety (HYV) seeds**, chemical fertilizers, and irrigation techniques.
 
• It transformed India into a nation self-sufficient in food grains, especially **wheat and rice**.
 
• This revolution was led by **Dr. M.S. Swaminathan**, known as the father of the Green Revolution in India.
 
• The Green Revolution also had a major impact on reducing **famine risks** and improving **food security**.
 
 
 
• **Yellow Revolution**__
 
 
• The **Yellow Revolution** in India is associated with the **production and growth of edible oil**, particularly **mustard and sunflower oil**.
 
• It aimed to reduce India's dependence on imported edible oils and achieve **self-reliance** in oilseed production.
 
• The revolution focused on improving **oilseed cultivation techniques** and promoting the use of **hybrid varieties**.
 
• The Yellow Revolution also supported rural livelihoods by enhancing **oilseed farming** opportunities.

questions.question: Effective Revenue Deficit was introduced in the government budgeting during which year?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is__ 2011-12__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Effective Revenue Deficit** was introduced in **2011-12** during the **Union Budget of India**.
 
• The concept was introduced to distinguish between revenue expenditure that creates assets and other types of revenue expenditure.
 
• It is calculated by subtracting the **Grants for Creation of Capital Assets** from the Revenue Deficit.
 
• This measure was introduced to give a clearer picture of the actual deficit that impacts the fiscal position of the government.
 
• The **primary goal** of Effective Revenue Deficit is to promote transparency in public finance and encourage capital asset creation.
 
• It helps in understanding how much of the revenue expenditure is contributing to the creation of assets, which is a long-term benefit for the economy.
 
• This concept aligns with the government's efforts to improve fiscal discipline and ensure efficient allocation of resources.
 
• It is significant for policymakers and economists as it provides insights into the government's financial health and investment in infrastructure and development projects.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• ** 2003-04**__

 __
 
• The year **2003** is significant in Indian fiscal policy due to the introduction of the **Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management (FRBM) Act**.
 
• The FRBM Act aims to ensure responsible fiscal management and reduce fiscal deficits.
 
• It laid down targets for reducing the **Revenue Deficit** and **Fiscal Deficit**, but it did not include the concept of Effective Revenue Deficit.
 
 
 
• **2015-16**__
 __
 
• The year **2015-16** is associated with several fiscal reforms, but the concept of Effective Revenue Deficit was already introduced prior to this period.
 
• During this time, the government focused on fiscal consolidation and initiatives like **Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana (PMGSY)**.
 
 
 
• **2008-09**__
 
 
• The year **2008-09** marked the global financial crisis, which impacted India's economy.
 
• India launched various fiscal stimulus packages to boost economic growth during this period, but the Effective Revenue Deficit concept was introduced later in **2011-12**.

questions.question: Udyami Bharat, MUDRA Yojana, Emergency Credit Line Guarantee Scheme, SFURTI and RAMP schemes are associated with the development of which sector?

• Annual Turnover: up to ₹10 crore
 
 
 
• **Small Enterprise**
 
 
• Investment in Plant & Machinery/Equipment: up to ₹25 crore
 
• Annual Turnover: up to ₹100 crore
 
 
 
• Medium Enterprise

• Annual Turnover: up to ₹500 crore
 
 

 

 
• **Significance of MSMEs:**

• Contribution to Manufacturing Output: Nearly 45% of the total manufacturing output.
 
• Contribution to Exports: About 40–45% of India’s total exports.

• MSMEs are critical for promoting balanced regional development and reducing income disparities.
 
 
 
• **Challenges faced by MSMEs:**
 
 
• Limited access to credit and financial support.
 
• Inadequate infrastructure and technology adoption.
 
• High compliance costs and lack of skilled labor.
 
 
 
• **Government Initiatives for MSMEs:**
 
 
• **Atmanirbhar Bharat:** Focuses on self-reliance and includes MSME sector reforms.
 
• **Digital MSME:** Promotes IT adoption to enhance competitiveness.
 
• **Zero Defect Zero Effect (ZED):** Encourages quality manufacturing with minimal environmental impact.

questions.question: Which statistical indicator is used to measure the depth of poverty by accounting for the extent to which individuals fall below the poverty line?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Poverty Gap Index**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Poverty Gap Index** measures the intensity of poverty by calculating the average shortfall of incomes of the poor relative to the poverty line.
 
• It highlights the depth of poverty by determining how far individuals fall below the poverty line on average.
 
• The Poverty Gap Index is expressed as a proportion of the poverty line, making it a useful tool for comparing poverty across different regions or countries.
 
• A higher Poverty Gap Index indicates deeper poverty, showing that the poor are further away from the poverty threshold.
 
• This index is widely used in socio-economic studies for policy formulation aimed at poverty alleviation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gini Coefficient:**

 
 
• A measure of income inequality within a population, ranging from 0 (perfect equality) to 1 (perfect inequality).
 
• It does not account for poverty depth or distribution below the poverty line.
 
 
 
• **Headcount Ratio:**
 
 
• Represents the proportion of the population living below the poverty line.
 
• It is a simple measure but does not provide information about the intensity or depth of poverty.
 
 
 
• **Dependency Ratio:**
 
 
• The ratio of dependents (people aged below 15 and above 64) to the working-age population.
 
• It is used to analyze demographic and economic burdens but is unrelated to poverty measurement.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Poverty Metrics:**
 
 
• Poverty metrics like the Poverty Gap Index help policymakers design targeted interventions for poverty reduction.
 
• They provide insights into not just the prevalence but also the severity of poverty.

questions.question: The Capital Adequacy Ratio, sometimes seen in news, is related to which of the following?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Banking operations**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Capital Adequacy Ratio (CAR)** is a metric used to measure the **financial strength of banks**, ensuring they have enough capital to absorb potential losses.
 
• It is expressed as a percentage of a bank's risk-weighted credit exposures, calculated using Tier 1 and Tier 2 capital.
 
• CAR is mandated by international banking regulations such as the Basel Accords, which promote financial stability and reduce systemic risks.
 
• The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) requires Indian banks to maintain a minimum CAR of 9%, higher than the Basel III global standard of 8%.
 
• The ratio ensures banks can sustain operations even during financial crises, safeguarding depositors' interests and maintaining trust in the banking system.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Basel Accords:**

 
 
• International banking regulatory frameworks developed by the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision.
 
• Basel I (1988), Basel II (2004), and Basel III (2010) focus on improving risk management and enhancing financial stability.
 
• Basel III introduced stricter CAR requirements, liquidity coverage ratios, and leverage ratios.
 
 
 
• **Tier 1 and Tier 2 Capital:**
 
 
• Tier 1 capital consists of core capital like equity and disclosed reserves, which can absorb losses directly.
 
• Tier 2 capital includes supplementary capital such as subordinated debt and undisclosed reserves.
 
• Banks use both types of capital to calculate CAR, with Tier 1 being more critical for financial stability.
 
 
 
• **Risk-Weighted Assets (RWA):**
 
 
• Assets are assigned risk weights based on their inherent credit, market, and operational risks.
 
• For example, government securities may have a lower risk weight compared to loans to businesses.
 
• RWA calculations are crucial for determining CAR and compliance with regulatory standards.
 
 
 
• **Importance of CAR:**
 
 
• Maintains depositor confidence by ensuring banks are financially stable.
 
• Helps mitigate risks of insolvency during economic downturns.
 
• Promotes responsible lending and banking practices.

questions.question: What was the average annual growth rate of industries comprising mining, manufacturing and electricity during the post-reform period between 1991-92 and 2011- 12?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**6.7%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The average annual growth rate of industries comprising **mining, manufacturing, and electricity** during the post-reform period (1991-92 to 2011-12) was recorded at **6.7%**.
 
• This growth reflects the structural changes in the Indian economy following the implementation of the **1991 economic reforms**, which included liberalization, privatization, and globalization.
 
• Among the industrial sectors, manufacturing exhibited robust growth, while mining faced challenges due to environmental and regulatory issues.
 
• The electricity sector also witnessed significant growth during this period, driven by **increased power generation capacity** and reforms in the energy sector.
 
• The higher growth rate of the industrial sector contributed significantly to India's overall GDP growth during the post-reform period.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **1991 Economic Reforms:**

 
 
• These reforms marked a shift from a mixed economy to a market-oriented economy in India.
 
• Key measures included **reducing import tariffs, deregulating markets, and reducing the role of public sector enterprises**.
 
• The reforms aimed to address the balance of payments crisis and boost economic growth.
 
 
 
• **Industrial Sector Breakdown:**
 
 
• **Mining:** Contributed significantly to raw material supply but faced challenges in sustainability and environmental compliance.
 
• **Manufacturing:** Benefited from increased foreign direct investment (FDI), technological advancements, and policy support.
 
• **Electricity:** Growth was fueled by infrastructure investments and reforms in the energy sector, such as the Electricity Act of 2003.
 
 
 
• **Electricity Act, 2003:**
 
 
• Introduced reforms to promote competition, efficiency, and private sector participation in the power sector.
 
• Facilitated the development of renewable energy and increased power generation capacity.
 
 
 
• **Impact on GDP:**
 
 
• The industrial sector contributed substantially to India’s GDP growth, averaging around **27%-30% of GDP** during this period.
 
• This growth was instrumental in reducing poverty levels and creating employment opportunities in India.

questions.question: Per capita income is an indicator of economic development. What happened to India’s per capita income post 1991 economic reforms?

__
 
• Post the **1991 economic reforms in India**, the country witnessed a significant rise in its **per capita income**. These reforms included liberalization, privatization, and globalization, which boosted economic growth.
 
• The reforms dismantled the **License Raj system**, removed trade barriers, and attracted **foreign direct investment (FDI)**, leading to higher industrial and service sector output.
 
• The growth in sectors like **information technology, pharmaceuticals, and services** played a crucial role in increasing income levels.
 
• The reforms also led to the creation of new employment opportunities, enhancing the overall purchasing power and improving the **standard of living**.
 
• India's **GDP growth rate** surged during this period, often achieving an average growth rate of 6-8% annually, which directly impacted the per capita income.
 
• The rise in per capita income reflects the improved distribution of economic benefits among the population, even though disparities remained in certain regions.
 
• Key government measures, such as tax reforms and financial sector liberalization, further contributed to economic stability and growth.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Declined sharply**__

 __
 
• This option is incorrect because the 1991 reforms brought significant economic growth, not a decline. However, there was a short-term impact due to initial adjustments but no long-term sharp decline in per capita income.

 __
 
• The per capita income did not remain stagnant. The liberalization policies ensured that the economy grew at a steady pace, leading to consistent increases in income levels.
 
 
 
• **Became negative**__

questions.question: In which year did the government notify the New Public Sector Enterprise (PSE) Policy for Atma Nirbhar Bharat, that provides overall guidance on strategic disinvestment, and intends to minimise the presence of Government in PSEs across all sectors of economy?

• This policy is aligned with the vision of **Atma Nirbhar Bharat**, which aims to make India self-reliant across various sectors.
 
• The policy provides **guidance on strategic disinvestment** and seeks to reduce the presence of the government in **Public Sector Enterprises (PSEs)** across all sectors of the economy.
 
• It emphasizes that the **Government will only retain PSEs** in strategic sectors, while in non-strategic sectors, **PSEs will either be privatized or closed.**
 
• The strategic sectors identified under the policy include areas such as **atomic energy, defense, transport, telecommunications, banking, and insurance.**
 
• The policy supports the Government’s effort to **optimize resource allocation**, enhance efficiency, and facilitate growth by allowing private sector participation in industries previously dominated by the public sector.
 
• Strategic disinvestment and privatization under the policy aim to unlock the potential of PSEs by improving their **competitiveness, profitability, and operational efficiency.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• While **2023** is a recent year, the **New Public Sector Enterprise Policy** was already notified earlier in **2021**.

questions.question: What is the tenure of the Central Board of Directors in Reserve Bank of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Four years**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The tenure of the Central Board of Directors of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) is **four years**.
 
• The Central Board of Directors is the highest decision-making body of the RBI, responsible for the bank's overall supervision and direction.
 
• It is constituted as per the provisions of the **Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934**.
 
• The Central Board of Directors consists of the Governor, Deputy Governors, and other members appointed by the Government of India.
 
• The tenure of these members ensures continuity in decision-making and stability in the functioning of the RBI.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Reserve Bank of India (RBI):** The RBI is India's central banking institution, established on **1 April 1935**, under the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934.
 
• **Composition of the Central Board:** It includes the Governor, four Deputy Governors, and 10 non-official directors nominated by the government, along with other members as per the Act.
 
• **Functions of the Board:** The Central Board formulates policies for the regulation of the issuance of currency, management of foreign exchange, and ensuring monetary stability in the country.
 
• **Legal Framework:** The RBI operates under the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934, and the Banking Regulation Act, 1949.
 
• **Importance of Tenure:** A four-year tenure provides the board members sufficient time to implement policies effectively, ensuring long-term economic and financial stability.

questions.question: Disinvestment proceeds contribute to non-tax revenue of the government. Which body manages disinvestment in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**DIPAM**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Department of Investment and Public Asset Management (DIPAM)** is the nodal agency in India for managing disinvestment and strategic sale of public sector enterprises (PSEs).
 
• DIPAM operates under the **Ministry of Finance** and is responsible for generating revenue through the sale of government stakes in public sector companies.
 
• The department was earlier known as the **Department of Disinvestment** before being renamed as DIPAM in 2016.
 
• DIPAM's objective is to ensure optimal realization from the sale of government equity in central public sector enterprises (CPSEs).
 
• It also oversees the management of assets of public sector enterprises, including those earmarked for disinvestment.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Disinvestment:**

 
 
• It refers to the process of selling or liquidating the government’s stake in public sector undertakings (PSUs).
 
• The primary objective of disinvestment is to raise resources for the government and improve the operational efficiency of PSUs.
 
• Disinvestment proceeds are part of the non-tax revenue of the government.
 
 
 
• **Strategic Disinvestment:**
 
 
• It involves the sale of substantial portions of government equity in a PSU, often to private entities, along with the transfer of management control.
 
• Strategic disinvestment aims to bring in private sector expertise and investment for better management and growth of PSUs.
 
 
 
• **DIPAM’s Key Functions:**
 
 
• Formulating policies related to disinvestment and asset monetization.
 
• Advising the government on the timing and mode of disinvestment.
 
• Overseeing the listing of CPSEs on stock exchanges to unlock their value.
 
 
 
• **Examples of Recent Disinvestments:**
 
 
• Major disinvestment cases include the strategic sale of Air India, LIC IPO, and BPCL disinvestment.
 
• These initiatives aim to bridge the fiscal deficit and promote a self-reliant India.

questions.question: What was the unemployment rate in India as per the Periodic Labour Force Survey during January to December 2024?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**3.2%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The unemployment rate in India during January to December 2024 was recorded at **3.2%** according to the Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS).
 
• This figure represents a **decrease in unemployment rates** compared to previous years, indicating an improvement in the labor market.
 
• The PLFS, conducted by the **National Statistical Office (NSO)**, is the key survey for tracking unemployment and labor force participation in India.
 
• Rural unemployment stood at a **lower level** compared to urban areas, reflecting the differences in employment opportunities in these regions.
 
• The survey highlights a **rise in self-employment** and informal sector jobs, contributing to the decline in the unemployment rate.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS):**

 
 
• Launched by the NSO in 2017, PLFS is India’s official household-based employment survey.
 
• It provides data on key labor market indicators like unemployment, workforce participation, and labor force participation rates.
 
 
 
• **Unemployment Rate:**
 
 
• Defined as the percentage of people in the labor force who are unemployed and actively seeking employment.
 
• This is a key indicator of economic health and labor market conditions.
 
 
 
• **Urban vs Rural Employment:**
 
 
• Urban areas typically see higher unemployment rates due to reliance on formal sector jobs.
 
• Rural areas often have lower rates due to the prevalence of agricultural and informal work.
 
 
 
• **Labor Force Participation Rate (LFPR):**
 
 
• The proportion of the population aged 15 years and above that is either working or actively seeking work.
 
• India’s LFPR has historically been lower than global averages, especially for women.
 
 
 
• **Self-Employment in India:**
 
 
• A significant portion of India’s workforce is engaged in self-employment, particularly in agriculture, trade, and small-scale industries.
 
• Self-employment contributes to reducing unemployment but often involves low-income and unstructured work.

questions.question: India adopted a policy of Import Substitution Industrialisation (ISI) after independence. Which of the following was a common limitation faced by ISI-led strategy by the 1980s?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Technological backwardness**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• By the 1980s, India’s Import Substitution Industrialisation (ISI) strategy faced significant limitations such as **technological backwardness**, which hindered productivity and competitiveness.
 
• The focus on domestic production led to **limited access to advanced global technologies**, impacting innovation and modernization.
 
• Many industries under ISI were protected by high tariffs, creating a **lack of incentive to innovate or improve efficiency**.
 
• Technological stagnation resulted in **poor quality of goods** and inability to meet international standards, further limiting exports.
 
• Countries relying on ISI strategies often struggled with **low industrial diversification**, exacerbating technological deficiencies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Import Substitution Industrialisation (ISI):**

 
 
• ISI is an economic policy aimed at reducing dependency on imports by promoting domestic production of goods.
 
• It was widely adopted by developing countries post-World War II to foster industrial growth and economic independence.
 
 
 
• **Protectionism in ISI:**
 
 
• High import tariffs and quotas were imposed to protect domestic industries.
 
• While it encouraged initial industrial growth, it often led to inefficiency and lack of global competitiveness.
 
 
 
• **Technological Stagnation:**
 
 
• Limited investment in research and development under ISI policies contributed to technological backwardness.
 
• Dependence on outdated technologies restricted productivity and innovation.
 
 
 
• **Shift to Liberalization:**
 
 
• India began liberalizing its economy in 1991, moving away from ISI towards globalization and free-market policies.
 
• This shift aimed to integrate India into the global economy and encourage technological advancements through foreign investments.

questions.question: Uninterrupted and seamless chain of Input Tax Credit (ITC) is a mechanism to avoid cascading of taxes in which of the following taxes?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**GST**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Goods and Services Tax (GST)** is a unified indirect tax system implemented in India to **eliminate cascading effects of taxation**.
 
• The concept of **Input Tax Credit (ITC)** under GST allows businesses to claim credit for the tax paid on purchases and use it to offset the tax liability on sales.
 
• GST ensures an **uninterrupted and seamless chain of Input Tax Credit**, reducing the tax burden at each stage of value addition.
 
• ITC under GST is applicable to **both goods and services**, aligning with the “One Nation, One Tax” principle.
 
• This mechanism improves compliance, ensures transparency, and helps in making products and services more competitive in the market.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Cascading Tax Effect:**

 
 
• Occurs when tax is levied on a product at every stage of production without credit for the taxes paid in the earlier stages.
 
• GST eliminates this issue by enabling ITC throughout the supply chain.
 
 
 
• **Input Tax Credit (ITC):**
 
 
• ITC allows taxpayers to deduct the tax paid on inputs from the tax payable on final output.
 
• Conditions for availing ITC include possession of tax invoice, receipt of goods/services, and payment of tax to the government.
 
 
 
• **GST Structure:**
 
 
• GST comprises Central GST (CGST), State GST (SGST), and Integrated GST (IGST).
 
• ITC is transferable between CGST and SGST/IGST under specific rules.
 
 
 
• **Benefits of GST:**
 
 
• Creates a unified tax structure across India, boosting ease of doing business.
 
• Reduces tax evasion by integrating tax systems digitally.
 
• Promotes transparency and reduces litigation in tax administration.

questions.question: In which state is the shifting agriculture known as ‘Jhum’?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Assam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• 'Jhum' is the local name for **shifting cultivation** practiced predominantly in the northeastern states of India, including Assam.
 
• It involves clearing a patch of forest land, burning the vegetation, and using the ash as fertilizer to grow crops.
 
• After cultivating the land for a few years, farmers leave it fallow to allow the soil to regain its fertility.
 
• Jhum cultivation is a traditional practice among tribal communities and is deeply rooted in their culture and livelihood.
 
• This agricultural method is also practiced in other northeastern states like Nagaland, Meghalaya, and Arunachal Pradesh, but Assam remains one of the prominent regions for Jhum cultivation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Shifting Cultivation:** It is an agricultural practice where land is cultivated temporarily, then abandoned to allow natural vegetation to regenerate.
 
• **Environmental Concerns:** Jhum cultivation has been criticized for causing deforestation, soil erosion, and loss of biodiversity in the northeastern states.
 
• **Sustainable Alternatives:** The Indian government and various NGOs promote sustainable agricultural practices like terrace farming as alternatives to Jhum cultivation.
 
• **Historical Significance:** Shifting cultivation has been practiced for centuries by indigenous communities, who rely on it for subsistence farming.
 
• **Government Initiatives:** Programs like the National Mission for Sustainable Agriculture (NMSA) aim to provide support to farmers transitioning from Jhum cultivation to more sustainable methods.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements regarding the Industrial Sector in India is/are correct?

1. According to National Manufacturing Policy 2011, every job created in the manufacturing sector creates two-three additional jobs in related activities.

2. Industries add value to the existing goods and also to the skill of labour employed in it; therefore, this sector is also considered a transformational sector.

3. As industries employ a large part of the population, industrial development is one of the preconditions for the eradication of unemployment and poverty from our country.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 2: 1, 2 and 3**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **National Manufacturing Policy 2011:** It highlights that every job created in the manufacturing sector leads to the creation of 2-3 additional jobs in related activities, emphasizing the multiplier effect of manufacturing employment.
 
• **Transformational Sector:** Industries add value to raw materials and enhance the skill set of workers, which is why the industrial sector is considered a transformational sector in economic development.
 
• **Employment & Poverty Eradication:** Industrial development plays a critical role in generating employment and is a precondition for eradicating poverty and unemployment in India.
 
• The industrial sector contributes significantly to the Gross Domestic Product (GDP) and serves as a backbone for the economic progress of the country.
 
• Policies like Make in India and National Manufacturing Policy aim to boost industrial growth and employment generation in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Industrial Sector Overview:**

 
 
• The industrial sector includes manufacturing, construction, mining, and utilities.
 
• It is a key driver of economic growth, accounting for approximately 25-30% of India’s GDP.
 
 
 
• **National Manufacturing Policy (NMP) 2011:**
 
 
• Aimed at increasing the share of manufacturing in GDP to 25% by 2022.
 
• Focuses on skill development, technology upgrades, and creation of National Investment and Manufacturing Zones (NIMZs).
 
 
 
• **Make in India Initiative:**
 
 
• Launched in September 2014 to promote manufacturing and attract foreign investments.
 
• Targets 25 priority sectors including automobiles, pharmaceuticals, and textiles.
 
 
 
• **Employment in Industrial Sector:**
 
 
• Accounts for a large segment of formal and informal employment in India.
 
• Industrial policies aim to reduce unemployment through job creation in manufacturing and allied sectors.
 
 
 
• **Challenges in Industrial Development:**
 
 
• Infrastructure bottlenecks, skill gaps, and regulatory hurdles.
 
• Low levels of research and development (R&D) and technological innovation.

questions.question: To promote agricultural exports and global competitiveness, reforms were extended to the agricultural sector as well. Which of the following initiatives aims to create a seamless national market for agricultural commodities?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**e-NAM**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **e-NAM (National Agriculture Market)** is a pan-India electronic trading platform launched by the **Government of India on April 14, 2016**, under the Ministry of Agriculture.
 
• The platform aims to integrate agricultural markets across the country, providing farmers with better price discovery and reducing the need for middlemen.
 
• e-NAM facilitates online trading of agricultural commodities, enabling farmers to sell their produce directly to buyers in a transparent manner.
 
• It connects existing Agricultural Produce Market Committees (APMCs) and other market yards into a unified network, ensuring a seamless national market for agricultural commodities.
 
• As of 2023, e-NAM has onboarded more than 1,000 mandis (markets) across India, significantly improving market access for farmers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Agricultural Produce Market Committee (APMC) Act**

 
 
• The APMC Act governs the sale of agricultural produce in regulated markets (mandis).
 
• It aims to prevent exploitation of farmers by intermediaries but has been criticized for creating inefficiencies and limiting farmers' ability to sell freely.
 
• Many states have amended the APMC Act to allow direct marketing, contract farming, and private market establishment.
 
 
 
• **PM-KISAN (Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi)**
 
 
• Launched in February 2019, PM-KISAN provides direct income support of ₹6,000 per year to small and marginal farmers.
 
• The amount is paid in three equal installments of ₹2,000 each.
 
• This scheme aims to ensure financial stability for farmers and improve agricultural productivity.
 
 
 
• **Kisan Credit Card (KCC)**
 
 
• Introduced in 1998 by NABARD, the Kisan Credit Card scheme provides farmers with timely access to credit for agricultural and allied activities.
 
• It offers flexible repayment options and ensures liquidity for farmers during crucial farming periods.
 
 
 
• **e-NAM Features**
 
 
• Allows farmers to check real-time commodity prices and sell their produce at the best available rates.
 
• Facilitates payment directly to farmers' bank accounts, reducing delays and corruption.
 
• Promotes transparency and efficiency in agricultural trade by reducing market inefficiencies.
 
 

15

questions.question: Post 1991 economic reforms, India witnessed significant changes in the banking sector. What is one major reform introduced in the banking sector?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Deregulation of interest rates**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Deregulation of interest rates **was a key reform introduced in the Indian banking sector as part of the **post-1991 economic reforms**.
 
• Prior to this, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) tightly regulated interest rates, but deregulation allowed banks to determine interest rates based on market conditions.
 
• This reform enhanced competition among banks, resulting in better services and improved financial efficiency.
 
• LiberalCreation approved financials to meet diverse customer demands to compete on deposits and loans
 
• It aimed to develop a more flexible and market-driven banking system, which was crucial for India's transition to a more liberalized economy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR):**

 
 
• SLR is the percentage of a bank's net demand and time liabilities (NDTL) that must be maintained in liquid assets like cash, gold, or government-approved securities before providing credit to customers.
 
• It is used by the RBI to control inflation and regulate the credit flow in the economy.
 
 
 
• **Repo Rate and Reverse Repo Rate:**
 
 
• The repo rate is the rate at which the RBI lends money to commercial banks, while the reverse repo rate is the rate at which RBI borrows money from banks.
 
• These tools are used to control liquidity and inflation in the economy.
 
 
 
• **Banking Sector Liberalization:**
 
 
• Reforms after 1991 allowed the entry of private and foreign banks into India, leading to growth and innovation in services.
 
• This also led to significant investments in technology, improving efficiency and customer experience.
 
 
 
• **Non-Performing Assets (NPAs):**
 
 
• NPAs are loans or advances where the borrower has stopped making interest or principal repayments for a specified period.
 
• The banking reforms also aimed to address the issue of rising NPAs through better credit risk management and recovery mechanisms.
